book: 118 - Scott Adams and Philosophy - A Hole in the Fabric of Reality

chapters.file: ch07 - The Reality of Scott Adams.md
chapters.relation: The editors' introduction sets up the book: in 2016 Scott Adams, a left-leaning Mensa member trained in hypnosis, predicted a 98-percent Trump landslide on the ground that Trump is a rare Master Persuader whose outrageous statements were calibrated weapons-grade persuasion aimed at irrational, emotion-driven voters who rationalize after the fact, and that the victory would rip a hole in the fabric of reality, producing cognitive dissonance and mass hysteria among Hillary supporters. It then profiles Adams's path from bank teller and 4 a.m. cartoonist at Pacific Bell to Dilbert creator, business guru (The Dilbert Principle and the Logitech gibberish mission-statement prank in a false mustache), fiction writer (God's Debris, The Religion War), talent-stack theorist of How to Fail at Almost Everything and Still Win Big, and author of Win Bigly, framing the volume as philosophy's examination of this gadfly.

chapters.file: ch08 - I. In Front of Your Eyes.md
ch09 - 1. How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Tolerate the Master Persuader Hypothesis.md
chapters.relation: Wolfe reads Adams's Master Persuader hypothesis through the ancient quarrel between Socrates and the Sophists: Derren Brown's deflation of hypnosis into one personality dominating another leads to Gorgias's Encomium of Helen, where persuasive words are magic spells that steal free will, and to Plato's Gorgias, where Socrates condemns rhetoric as cookery and cosmetics that flatter the ignorant while his disciple Polus covets its tyrannical power. On this mapping Trump's plain-talk style is simply Aristotle's available means of persuasion for a particular audience, and Adams is mostly a Sophist who treats words as programming code for moist robots, though he keeps a Socratic sliver in his stated aim of exposing readers to different ideas rather than converting them. Wolfe closes by refusing both readings of Adams as pro-Trump troll or alt-right hero, urging each side to see how persuasion actually worked on them.

chapters.file: ch10 - 2. Persuade Me Once, Shame on You . ..md
chapters.relation: Greene dismantles both phases of Adams's case that Trump is a Master Persuader. The trait-list phase (opening with big demands, the Intentional Wrongness Persuasion Play, never apologizing, exuding confidence, recruiting the reciprocity instinct, and the talent stack) fails because doing what master persuaders do is not being one, by the Tom Brady versus Archie Manning point that we never define good quarterbacks by wins alone and by the Kantian thought that an act must be done for the right reason. The reality phase borrows Plato, Hume, and Kant to deny us access to an objective world, but the chapter replies that the experts' predictive failures illustrate Hume's problem of induction rather than proving there are no facts, notes Adams even misreads Plato, and observes that nothing links the Persuasion Filter's one success to Trump's skills rather than to a one-off political climate.

chapters.file: ch11 - 3. How I Could Have Made Hillary President.md
chapters.relation: Taking Adams at his word that persuasion is learnable technique, Steele dissects Trump's linguistic kill shots (Low-energy Jeb, Crooked Hillary, Lyin' Ted, Pocahontas) as visual, confirmation-bias-proof forever names that killed Jeb Bush's candidacy in half a second, and contrasts the Clinton campaign's committee flops (Donald Duck, Dangerous Donald, Drumpf, and slogans like Love Trumps Hate and Stronger Together). He then practices what Adams preaches by drafting his own kill shot, The Don, a mafia frame built on offers that cannot be refused, omerta, and sleeping with the fishes, plus the slogan A Win-Win for America, engineered for positive repetition and the slightly-off meaning Adams calls intentional wrongness, concluding the election was winnable with commonsense marketing touches. An Orwell aside about whose victory a wartime poster really celebrates supplies the only classical rhetoric on display.

chapters.file: ch13 - 4. Scoundrels, the Lot of Us.md
chapters.relation: Karavitis finds a Hegelian dialectic in the three-panel Dilbert strip (thesis, antithesis, synthesis) delivered through irony, then tests that irony against philosophy: Socrates' feigned-ignorance questioning that leaves interlocutors in aporia, Hegel's complaint that irony is vanity withdrawing from objective reality, and Kierkegaard's dissertation on the concept of irony plus Either/Or, where irony is the bridge from the aesthetic to the ethical life. The punchline is that after nearly three decades of Dilbert the white-collar workplace has not changed, so readers who feel superior to their bosses and co-workers have taken the vain, narcissistic, aesthetic reading Hegel warned against, making the joke a scoundrelly way of avoiding responsibility. A Leo Strauss aside casts Adams as an esoteric writer whose irony preserves him from the powerful.

chapters.file: ch14 - 5. The Serious Point of Scott’s Humor.md
chapters.relation: Guerra and Barkman argue that Dilbert's humor is doing serious philosophical work: strips like the Pointy-Haired Boss's scheme to strip app users of free will, rebranded by Dilbert as marketing, distill manipulative corporate practice to its absurd essential core, and humor serves as a logical tool that, when it preserves the target's integrity rather than straw-manning it, exposes the equivocation in earnest arguments about getting something from nothing. They ground the practice in Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics, where wittiness is the virtuous mean between the vices of buffoonery and boorishness, read Adams's catalogue of failures and his luck-first, passion-is-bullshit account of success as a Socratic acknowledgment of ignorance that deflates the American Dream, and treat Win Bigly's persuasion lessons (visuals, repetition, intentional mistakes, the Hitler counterexample) as further proof that Adams has the virtue of wit.

In a sustained deadpan parody, Ketcham builds a conspiracy out of Ockham's Razor: William of Ockham's minimalist principle explains PowerPoint's big-type bullet points, but the slide deck (secretly engineered by DARPA with Microsoft, exported via Siberia to Putin) becomes a weapon that breeds stupidity, conditions Trump to tweet-length simplicities like fake news and crooked, and finally rigs him, not the voting machines. The chapter also wields the Razor correctly, insisting that a minimalist explanation must still be good and complete, as when little Jill's one bullet point tells us too little. Testing moral realism, Kant's absolute prohibition on lying, and utilitarianism's greatest happiness against the conspiracy's missing facts, it concludes we lack the information to render any moral verdict, which is exactly what the conspiracy-minded minimalists want.

chapters.file: ch16 - III. It Tastes Better if We All Do It Together.md
ch17 - 7. Scott Adams’s Joy of Logic.md
chapters.relation: Bilsker turns Adams's Joy of Work catalogue of irrational co-workers into a critical-thinking syllabus: faulty analogy (from dogs fetching sticks to potatoes dancing, and Francis Bacon's body-politic passage praising war as exercise), huge-pants faulty causation, the Reinhart-Rogoff debt paper that drove austerity policy on mere correlation until Herndon, Ash, and Pollin exposed it, complex and objectionable cause, the overapplication of Occam's Razor to moon-landing hoaxes, misplaced authority, begging the question, and egocentric biases like I Am the World. He then contrasts the classroom view that confirmation bias is an unconscious background program with Win Bigly's claim that bias is the operating system itself, worrying about the implication that reasoning with anyone is futile, and concludes that Adams overstates how incapable we are of overcoming our biases.

chapters.file: ch18 - 8. Is It a Fact that Facts Don’t Matter.md
chapters.relation: Steele distinguishes facts as mind-independent reality from facts as expert-certified statements to show that Kellyanne Conway's alternative facts and Adams's own slogans trade on this ambiguity, and that Adams performatively contradicts himself every time he insists his predictions are true and matter. Analyzing the cognitive-dissonance hallucinations of Trump-is-Hitler and then Trump-is-incompetent, he argues that on Adams's own account brute facts proved irresistible, and that such belief revision is rational Popperian conjecture and refutation, plus the conservative strategy of saving fundamental theories (Coulomb's law) and dropping minor ones when the fuse blows. Against the claim that humans are irrational he recalls Aristotle's Rhetoric as persuasion's legitimate complement to the Prior Analytics, and leans on Percival to show propaganda fits a rational-reader model, citing the slow, fact-driven shift on gay marriage.

Hansmann and Jones set Adams's gender posts against the four waves of feminism and the men's rights movement: his March 2011 Men's Rights post telling activists to get over it while lumping women with four-year-olds and the mentally handicapped, his Global Gender War matriarchy in which any country where women can vote counts as female-ruled, his framing of sex as a woman's currency for extracting male strategy (sacrifice a pawn to nail the queen), and his serial interrupting of women. They show the rhetoric eerily echoes anti-suffragists like Mrs. William Force Scott and Senator Sanford and the Goldilocks Dilemma, note the red-pill fantasy borrowed from The Matrix, and conclude that calling America a matriarchy defies scholarly consensus, with Beauvoir's The Second Sex marking why the vote never delivered the balance of power.

Saunders uses Adams's induhviduals and a hundred-voter dilution example in which smart people's votes are swamped to stage the classic case against democracy: Plato's physician analogy against Athenian rule by the ignorant and his philosopher-kings, Jason Brennan's hobbits, hooligans, and Vulcans with voter licensing, Mill's plural votes for the demonstrably wise, and Nussbaum's claim that humanities education breeds empathetic democratic citizens. Each fix fails on Dilbert's own terms, since competence tests demean the labeled, the Pointy-Haired Boss would amass extra votes while Dilbert-grade engineers lack political judgment, Asok's degree would not help, and the more educated are demographically skewed toward men. He concludes that equal votes win as a pragmatic default and muses that workplaces, not polities, might be the truer target of democratization.

Christian contrasts Camus's absurdity, the futile collision between our demand for meaning and a silent world whose only exits are suicide, a leap of faith, or Sisyphean revolt (an active defiance he takes partly from Nietzsche's rejection of resignation), with Adams's office absurdities. In Dilbert the absurd is contained and epistemic rather than pervasive and metaphysical: the battery-dead LED request, Dadaist mission statements, Catbert's evil HR policies, Wally's self-congratulatory Wally Reports, and Alice's harpoon all trace to people being idiots about different things, and could be fixed by honest credit and realizable plans. Dilbert's Business Dorky acceptance therefore looks Camusian but is not: it is recognition minus revolt, bewildered amusement where revolt and reform remain genuinely available.

chapters.file: ch23 - 12. Dilbert Is an Asshole and That’s Why He’ll Never Be Happy and Nobody Loves Him.md
chapters.relation: Elsby and Luzecky argue Dilbert's unhappiness is chosen: from 400 rejections he concludes the women lack quality, he calls insult-bombing gentle kidding, and when Dogbert cites man's rational essence he chooses to watch all-star wrestling, each a textbook Sartrean bad faith where he glimpses the truth and flees it. Measured against Aristotle's eudaimonia he lacks every virtue of the Nicomachean mean (courage as the midpoint of fear, rightly scaled ambition, wit), and since one swallow does not make a summer his whole life, not a day of it, could earn the name happy. The December 2017 addictive-app strips complete the verdict: Dilbert monetizes a zombie-making app for a raise, making him Beauvoir's serious man from The Ethics of Ambiguity, the intelligent sell-out who subordinates human value to a hierarchy he knows is hollow.

Knuths asks whether Dogbert is essentially a dog and only accidentally white, importing Aristotle's Metaphysics distinction between essential and accidental properties and its modern modal gloss: essences are what an object has in all possible worlds, with David Lewis's concrete-constructionist reading noted against the standard view of worlds as abstract sets of propositions. The puzzle is that Dogbert's 2014 stint as CEO, combined with his canine essence, would prove dogs can be CEOs, threatening absurd conclusions about the real world unless we choose an ontology of fiction. Three candidates are weighed without a verdict: possibilism (Adams discovered a possible world), Meinongianism (Dogbert has being without existence, at the cost of square circles), and creationism (Dogbert is Adams's abstract artifact, troubled by the Not-Adams duplicate-creator case).

chapters.file: ch25 - 14. Of Course It Sucks—It’s Work.md
chapters.relation: Wible stages three theories of work against Dilbert strips: the Greek view of Plato and Aristotle that labor is freedom-sapping and leisure is the civilized ideal, Marx's capitalist critique in which workers become objects and machines (Wally gives off no human vibe, and robots are coming for the engineers), and Desjardins's human-fulfillment model built on Schumacher's creativity, challenge, development, honesty, and beauty, with Wells Fargo's fake accounts showing how jobs that force lying corrupt character. He endorses instead a Kantian middle ground anchored in Norman Bowie's moral minimum: never treating workers as mere means, so the CEO making intern Asok drink industrial sludge on stage is a violation of respect for persons, not just bad management. Sisyphus supplies the image of pointless labor, though even he might be redeemed if he loved the rock.

chapters.file: ch26 - V. Golden Age, Ready or Not.md

chapters.relation: Percival, whose Myth of the Closed Mind Adams cites, rebuts the Moist Robot Hypothesis that visual, emotional, repetitive anchors make us ninety-percent irrational. Against Kahneman's fast-and-dumb System 1 he sets Gigerenzer's ecological rationality (the gaze-angle heuristic that catches fly balls, the recognition heuristic that lets ignorant German students beat Americans on Detroit versus Milwaukee), then goes further with Popper's critical rationalism: babies as little scientists conjecturing and refuting, experience always theory-laden (the duck-rabbit), and Newton's boy on the seashore facing an infinite but navigable ocean of error elimination. The Stoic insight that all emotion is thoughtful and all thought emotional (the falling-tiles misperception that flips anger to relief) shows feelings track beliefs, so a free battle of the biases, not fact-free affirmation in the lineage of Le Bon and Pavlovian conditioning, is how rationality actually works.

chapters.file: ch28 - 16. Why Scott Adams Is Stupid.md
chapters.relation: Miori audits Adams's science talk through epistemology: warrant for belief, empiricism versus rationalism, Wittgenstein's demand for unambiguous clarity, and Clifford's epistemic responsibility, that it is always wrong to believe on insufficient evidence, which condemns sampling television news while blogging on climate science. Popper's falsifiability, learned from Einstein's willingness to be refuted against Freud's confirmation-seeking, exposes Adams's double standard in waving confirmation bias at critics while crediting his own predictions, and Feyerabend's epistemological anarchism is the view Adams most resembles, except that Feyerabend took responsibility and retracted. Cipolla's Basic Laws of Human Stupidity (the stupid person causes losses to both self and others) frames the closing charge: Adams suggests and retreats, sells product, and shirks the epistemic duty that experts in climate science and medicine shoulder.

Robison-Greene reads God's Debris as a Socratic dialogue on speed: the Avatar, like Socrates after the Delphic oracle, guts the Postman's confidence so he can unlearn, and the whole book functions as a Cartesian skeptical hypothesis in the dream-and-evil-demon lineage, here that we are the dust of a self-destructed God and perception is illusion, with gravity re-described as probability. Her counterattack is that the cosmology commits category mistakes, since probability cannot cause dust to reappear any more than Joe can consist of tallness, and that God made of probability is incoherent even for an omnipotent being. The five levels of awareness collapse too: level-four skeptics are just people who trust reliable methods, and the Avatar's claim that the mind is an illusion generator is self-defeating, since his own omniscience presupposes objective truth.

chapters.file: ch30 - 18. Scott Adams and the Pinocchio Fallacy.md
chapters.relation: Steele attacks Adams's embrace of the simulation hypothesis with the Pinocchio fallacy: a wooden boy cannot even hanker to be real, because hankering is conscious and wood is the wrong kind of stuff, and likewise no amount of code yields experience, since a simulation of weather wets no one and Deep Blue never knew it was playing chess. Bostrom's careful argument is distinguished from its popularizers, whose substrate-independence slide smuggles possibility into actuality (by the same logic a block of wood could be conscious), and the Matrix storyline, read as an allegory of Marx's exploitation and ideology, is judged as untenable as its energy-harvesting plot. Consciousness remains a property of living bodies, replication rather than simulation, and even if software minds were possible, trapping them in a fabricated world would be immoral.

holes.name: Gorgias
holes.what: Sophist rhetorician whose Encomium of Helen likens persuasive speech to magic or drugs that rob listeners of free will.
holes.why: Chapter 9 builds its reading of Adams's Master Persuader hypothesis directly on Gorgias's claim that the right words reprogram an audience regardless of truth.

holes.name: Sophistic Rhetoric (persuasion vs. truth)
holes.what: The Sophistic doctrine, opposed by Socrates in the Gorgias and Phaedrus, that persuasive power over an audience matters independently of truth and can be used for moral improvement or mere flattery.
holes.why: Chapter 9's whole framework is the Socratic-versus-Sophistic dichotomy about rhetoric, and taxonomy.json has only Protagoras's relativism, not the rhetoric-versus-truth debate this book turns on.

holes.name: Confirmation Bias
holes.what: The unconscious tendency to seek and favor evidence that confirms one's existing beliefs while discounting disconfirming evidence.
holes.why: Chapters 17, 18, 27, and 28 all pivot on Adams's claim that bias is the human operating system, and the debate over whether that makes us irrational needs this concept, which taxonomy.json lacks.

holes.name: Jason Brennan
holes.what: Contemporary political philosopher who defends epistocracy, restricting or weighting the vote to the competent (his hobbits, hooligans, and Vulcans typology).
holes.why: Chapter 20 uses Brennan's voter-licensing proposal as the modern heir to Plato's attack on rule by the ignorant, at comparable length to Plato and Mill themselves.

holes.name: Ontology of Fictional Characters
holes.what: The debate over what fictional beings are: discovered possible worlds (possibilism), Meinongian nonexistent objects, or abstract artifacts created by authors (creationism).
holes.why: Chapter 24 exists to decide what Dogbert metaphysically is, and its possible-worlds machinery alone cannot capture the possibilism-Meinongianism-creationism dispute it surveys.

holes.name: William Kingdon Clifford
holes.what: Victorian mathematician-philosopher whose ethics of belief holds it is always and everywhere wrong to believe anything on insufficient evidence.
holes.why: Chapter 28 makes Clifford's epistemic responsibility the central standard by which Adams's climate-science pronouncements are judged irresponsible.
